title: Avalon Systems POC results review + tuning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot results after week 3 of Avalon Systems pilot. Focus on tokens/sec/$ metrics, caching savings seen for repeat queries, batching tradeoffs for endpoint latency, and recommended config for next sprint. Action items include running an end-to-end latency benchmark, sharing security and pricing docs, and updating cache TTL by feature set.
next_steps: Redwood to share detailed tokens/sec-per-$ spreadsheet and per-route breakdown (Jordan)
Customer to run supplied end-to-end latency script in staging and share logs (Tom)
Schedule deep-dive on security & compliance with Avalon security team (Priya/Jordan)
Adjust cache TTL for FAQ endpoint and measure hit rate (Sara)
Follow-up call in one week to review benchmark results
action_items: Jordan Kim: Share tokens-per-dollar workbook and recommended config by 2026-04-20
Tom Patel: Run end-to-end latency script and upload logs to shared drive by 2026-04-22
Priya Shah: Prepare security artifact pack (SOC2 summary, KMS notes) by 2026-04-21
Sara Lopez: Implement cache TTL change on /faq route and report hit rate by 2026-04-22
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-18 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood), Mike Chen (Avalon CTO), Sara Lopez (ML Eng), Tom Patel (DevOps), Anika Roy (Product)

Summary: quick recap of week 3 pilot numbers, digging into where tokens/sec/$ came from and what caching bought us. Lots of tradeoff talk re: batching vs 95th pct latency.

[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, we'll kick off, quick agenda — results, tuning, and next steps. mike you okay to start with a quick context?
[00:18] Mike Chen: yeah thanks, jordan. week three ran, we saw the uplift on FAQ and the chat snippet but some of the longer form generation routes spiked costs so we wanna understand unit econ.
[00:34] Sara Lopez: to add, our baseline was about 1.2 tokens per ms maybe, uh that is noisy, but we observed caching for FAQ saved a lot, like 30-45% tokens per dollar effective, roughly.
[00:50] Priya Shah: cool, when you say tokens per dollar are you using the per-token billing from hosted or are you normalizing to throughput? just wanna align the metric.
[01:05] Tom Patel: we're normalizing to dollars spent on the Redwood hosted pilot credit tranche, so tokens / $ is total tokens generated divided by consumed credits converted to $ via the sheet.
[01:20] Jordan Kim: perfect, we sent an initial workbook last week, i'll share the deep spreadsheet after this call. quick preview — tokens/sec/$ is heavily shaped by sequence length distribution and KV cache hit rates.
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: example we saw: FAQ endpoint has short prompts, high cache hit -> effective tokens per dollar ~ 2.5x higher than the longform summarization route where caching is low.
[02:00] Sara Lopez: i wanted to highlight one oddity, the summarization route's throughput dropped mid-week when we hit bursts — seems batching policy switched to larger micro-batches and latency snafued.
[02:18] Priya Shah: that sounds like autoscaling + batching threshold interaction. we default to a batching window of 20ms for that model in the pilot, when burst arrives batching groups are larger which raises token efficiency but increases tail latency.
[02:35] Anika Roy: our SLA is 300ms p95 for interactive features, if batching pushes p95 above that users notice. we care about tokens/$ but not at expense of UX.
[02:50] Jordan Kim: absolutely. so tradeoff matrix — lower batching window gives better p95 but worse tokens/$, larger window reduces cost but hurts p95. we can do dynamic per-route batching tied to traffic profile.
[03:10] Mike Chen: is that something we can do in dedicated? or only hosted?
[03:20] Priya Shah: both. with Dedicated you can pin capacity and have more control over batching and kernel selection; hosted supports per-route policies too but there's more automatic routing. for your burst patterns dedicated gives the most predictable p95.
[03:40] Tom Patel: curious on caching — the FAQ route had a 62% hit rate last week per the demo, is that real?
[03:50] Jordan Kim: yes, our KV/prefix cache showed roughly 58-66% for FAQ depending on TTL. that hit rate translates to token savings because we avoid re-computing context.
[04:10] Sara Lopez: we experimented with TTL 5m vs 30m; 30m bumped hit rate but stale data concerns. we need a pragmatic TTL per feature.
[04:25] Priya Shah: suggestion: tiered TTLs — short TTL for high-churn endpoints, extended TTL for docs/FAQ. we can also implement cache invalidation hook from your CMS to purge on update.
[04:40] Anika Roy: yes push invalidation is a requirement.
[04:46] Jordan Kim: noted.
[05:00] [-- 5 minute mark - discussion shifts to numbers --]
[05:05] Jordan Kim: i'll read a couple numbers: overall tokens/$ for week 3 across all routes was 12.8k tokens per dollar, FAQ was 28k tokens/$, summarization 6.5k tokens/$. these are rough with noise.
[05:30] Sara Lopez: those FAQ numbers align with our expectation. summarization is killing us because of repeated long-context generations.
[05:45] Priya Shah: two levers here — prompt engineering to reduce context length, and micro-caching intermediate chunks for multi-turn summarization.
[06:00] Tom Patel: can you explain micro-caching?
[06:05] Priya Shah: e.g., cache embeddings or partial KV snapshots for segments so when you stitch you re-use computations instead of recomputing entire context. it's more infra work but can save tokens.
[06:20] Mike Chen: interesting. what's the expected saving ballpark?
[06:25] Liam O'Connor: depends on reuse rate, but in similar pilots we've seen 20-40% token savings for multi-turn summarization when micro-caching is feasible.
[06:38] Sara Lopez: we don't currently store intermediate embeddings, that's product work.
[06:45] Jordan Kim: ok flag for roadmap.
[06:50] [-- 10 minute mark - latency benchmark talk --]
[07:00] Jordan Kim: next item: latency benchmark. Tom you ran the smoke test last night?
[07:05] Tom Patel: yes i ran the basic curl script, attached in slack, but we need the end-to-end script that hits inference and traces kv hits.
[07:15] Priya Shah: we'll post the end-to-end script to the shared drive. it collects p50/p95/p99, batch sizes, and cache hit tags. please run it in your staging where traffic shape matches production.
[07:30] Tom Patel: plan to run it this afternoon.
[07:34] Jordan Kim: also capture CPU/GPU utilization and queue wait time if possible.
[07:40] Sara Lopez: question about quantization — we saw a small quality delta when using 4-bit in lab, any guidance?
[07:48] Priya Shah: quantization aggressiveness trades quality for throughput. for customer-facing summarization we recommend PTQ-8 or q4_0 as a middle ground; for internal batch jobs aggressive 4-bit is fine. can run evals against your golden set.
[08:05] Mike Chen: evals — we need Redwood to run a pass vs our golden summaries to quantify ROUGE/semantic drift.
[08:12] Jordan Kim: yes we can run that. please share the eval set and thresholds.
[08:18] [-- 15 minute mark - billing and credits --]
[08:30] Jordan Kim: regarding pilot credits and billing — current hosted consumption estimate projects a jump in month 2 if we don't change caching/batching. i propose a two-week cost mitigation sprint focusing on TTLs, prompt compression, and micro-caching prototype.
[08:48] Sara Lopez: that sounds good. can you be explicit on expected tokens/$ lift if we do all three?
[08:55] Liam O'Connor: bounded estimate: combined might get you +30-60% tokens/$ on routes amenable to caching; longform routes lower impact.
[09:10] Tom Patel: any vendor lock-in concerns with caching approaches?
[09:15] Priya Shah: cache design is application-level; Redwood's prefix/KV cache is pluggable — you can implement with your Redis or rely on Redwood-managed cache in hosted. no lock-in to model.
[09:30] Mike Chen: OK. about security, we need KMS integration notes and audit log retention — can we get a short doc?
[09:38] Priya Shah: yes; i'll bundle SOC2 summary, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logging details.
[09:45] Jordan Kim: expected to share by Wednesday.
[09:50] Anika Roy: one ask — can we get an estimate of tokens/sec/$ during peak vs steady? customers care about peaks.
[09:58] Jordan Kim: we'll output two slices in the workbook: steady-state tokens/sec/$ and peak tokens/sec/$ with corresponding p95.
[10:12] [-- 25 minute mark - technical deep dive request --]
[10:15] Sara Lopez: also want a technical deep dive on batching knobs and kernel selection, maybe next week.
[10:22] Priya Shah: happy to run that. we'll include demo of dynamic batching policy and how to map to p95 constraints.
[10:30] Mike Chen: will invite our infra team for that session.
[10:34] Jordan Kim: perfect.
[10:40] [-- 30 minute mark - misc issues --]
[10:45] Tom Patel: small note — we're seeing occasional mis-attribution of speaker labels in transcripts, not a blocker but FYI.
[10:52] Jordan Kim: thanks, we'll log that.
[10:55] Sara Lopez: one more on cost — can Redwood provide a suggested dedicated capacity configuration and cost estimate if we switch to Dedicated to stabilize p95?
[11:05] Liam O'Connor: yes we can model Dedicated with expected util and provide an amortized $/token estimate. that requires your expected RPS and peak concurrency numbers.
[11:20] Mike Chen: we can share RPS and concurrency after this call.
[11:28] Jordan Kim: great.
[11:30] [-- 40 minute mark - recap and action items --]
[11:35] Jordan Kim: recap: Jordan to send tokens/$ workbook and peak/steady slices; Priya to send security artifact pack and batching deep-dive invite; Tom to run latency script and share logs; Sara to change cache TTLs for FAQ and report hit rates; follow-up in one week.
[11:55] Mike Chen: all good, thanks.
[12:00] Jordan Kim: thanks team, see you next week.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (K V cash, V P C), speaker attribution sometimes generic due to recording.
questions: What is the expected tokens/$ lift if we apply TTL, prompt compression, and micro-caching?
Can Redwood run evals vs Avalon's golden set for quantization quality checks?
Is dynamic per-route batching possible on hosted or only on Dedicated?
